FOL: p_5(Nola) ⊕ (p_6(Nola) ⊕ p_12(Nola)) 
NL: Nola lays eggs if and only if either she has talons or she has feathers, but not both.

The mistake is in the logical structure. The natural language says "Nola lays eggs **if and only if** either she has talons or she has feathers, but not both." This is a biconditional: 
p_5(Nola) ↔ (p_6(Nola) ⊕ p_12(Nola))

But the FOL uses exclusive or (⊕) between p_5(Nola) and (p_6(Nola) ⊕ p_12(Nola)), which means:
"Nola lays eggs XOR (she has talons XOR feathers)" — which is not the same as a biconditional.

Since p ⊕ q is logically equivalent to ¬(p ↔ q), this FOL statement actually says the opposite of the intended biconditional.

Thus, this is a significant error in translation.
